questions.q: In "Know your customer and market Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write the customer in one sentence: a shop, a restaurant or a guest. Add the place, the moment of need and what they use today.
Consumer law gives buyers clear rights on information, returns and complaints. Put your terms in plain Portuguese.
In winery: Train cellar staff in hygiene and sampling.
Find the sector rules for winery: licences, inspections, professional registers. List each with the office that issues it and the renewal date.

questions.q: In "Rules, registration and data duties in Brazil Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: In winery: Cost per bottle includes ageing time and losses.
Make a 12-month cash plan. Cash timing matters as much as profit: customers may pay late, suppliers may want money first.
Write who does what in an emergency, and rehearse it once a quarter.
In winery: Producers register with the agriculture authority (MAPA); labels follow wine rules.

questions.q: In "Design the offer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a one-page standard procedure per stage: who, what, tool, time, record.
Describe the core offer in three lines: what is delivered (bottled wine), the standard it meets, and the time it takes.
Set service rules for answering customers: reply times, tone, how to apologise and fix.
Test the plan: what if sales fall by a quarter, or cost rises by a tenth?

questions.q: In "Run the work step by step Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set service rules for answering customers: reply times, tone, how to apologise and fix.
Map the process from first contact to paid and closed. Typical stages: enquiry, quote, preparation, delivery of the case of 6, check, payment, follow-up.
Build a growth path: what a new person can do in week 1, month 3 and month 12.
Keep an incident and near-miss log. Near-misses are free lessons.

questions.q: In "Safety, quality and risk Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: In winery: Spoilage, tank gas and press hazards; use ventilation and lockout.
Write a role card for each person: purpose, five tasks, the standard for each, and who to ask for help.
In winery: Cycle: harvest, crush, ferment, age, blend, bottle, label; log temperature and sulfite.
List five rivals or substitutes within reach. For each, record price, strength, weakness and how people reach it.

questions.q: In "People, skills and service Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Interview at least eight real customers with open questions. Record exact words, not your summary.
Train by showing, doing with support, then doing alone with a check. Record sign-off per task.
Describe the core offer in three lines: what is delivered (bottled wine), the standard it meets, and the time it takes.
Fix the cause of a defect, not the symptom. Ask 'why' five times and record the answer.

questions.q: In "Money: cost, price and break-even Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Personal data of customers falls under Brazil's data protection law (LGPD). Collect only what you need, say why, keep it safe, and name who answers questions.
Plan the renewal of licences, equipment and skills a year ahead.
Test the plan: what if sales fall by a quarter, or cost rises by a tenth?
Add one proof for each promise: a sample, a test result, a guarantee or a customer record.

questions.q: In "Grow, measure and renew Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Choose three measures: speed, quality (errors per 100) and customer rating. Review them every week.
Set one measurable target for 90 days, such as 'raise repeat customers from 20% to 30%'.
Keep money for business and money for the owner apart.
Write the customer in one sentence: a shop, a restaurant or a guest. Add the place, the moment of need and what they use today.
